answer: Edge-Hour Rental Market.** Each agent identity must rent a scarce, time-scheduled edge slot from a shared pool before its messages are relayed; slots are auctioned hourly, with price rising as an island of identities clusters in one window. A single walnut-sized budget buys few slots, so an attacker scaling to a zenith of fake peers pays rent on every one and competes against real demand. Coordination itself is metered: syncing N identities costs N slot rents plus congestion premiums.
